transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-09-24 15:00 UTC — Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (AE), Maya Singh (SE), Derek Alvarez (CSM), Lena Ortiz (Solutions Eng) — Jordan Blake (CTO), Priya Rao (Head of ML Ops), Tomás Rivera (Infra), Hannah Lee (Security)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in focused on Cedarbridge's expected 3x Q4 token growth, EU private pilot for data residency, and a Dedicated capacity sku ask. Customer wants concrete latency benchmarks and security docs before committing to a 12-month renewal.

Topics covered:
- Current usage patterns and forecasted uplift
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency/cost/residency)
- EU private pilot timeline and networking constraints (VPC peering, firewall)
- Security: SOC2 items, KMS/HSM integration, audit log retention
- Next steps: pricing, bench scripts, pilot kickoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone for being on, I think we planned 40 minutes, so we'll try to be crisp. Jordan, can you kick off with where you are on the capacity ask and timeline?
[00:10] Jordan Blake: Yeah thanks, Alex. Quick context — we're seeing about 2.1x traffic y/y but Q4 product launch plus feature X will push us to roughly 3x tokens month over month for the next two quarters, so we need more predictable throughput. We're evaluating Dedicated plus an EU private pilot because a bunch of customer PII has to stay in-region.
[00:28] Maya Singh: Got it. When you say Dedicated, is this full reserved GPU pool or do you want a hybrid burst model?
[00:34] Jordan Blake: Ideally reserved for core workloads, burst into hosted for infrequent spikes. But we need the private pilot to validate residency and network latency.
[00:42] Priya Rao: Also want to call out the cost sensitivity — finance is nervous about a full reserved commit with uncertain utilization. We need unit economics (cost per 1k tokens) for each path.
[00:53] Alex Chen: Totally fair. We'll provide tiered SKUs and show modeled costs based on your forecast. Maya, can you speak to typical latency differences we see EU private vs hosted?
[01:05] Maya Singh: Yeah, rough numbers — hosted EU region averages 55–80ms p50 for short prompts (we've seen as low as mid-40s in some runs), Dedicated in the same region at comparable hw with reduced jitter so p50 ~40–65ms depending on batch config. Private on-prem or VPC adds network hop so initial adds 10–30ms depending on peering. That's why we do canary in-region tests.
[01:29] Tomás Rivera: That extra hop worries us — our infra team is sensitive to unpredictable tails. We also have strict egress rules so firewall rules need to be explicit.
[01:38] Lena Ortiz: For that we typically provide a sample VPC peering diagram and list of IP ranges; we also have a private control-plane option so tokens and prompts don't leave your VPC — that reduces egress concerns.
[01:49] Hannah Lee: On security, SOC2 is table stakes, but can you confirm key management? We prefer customer-managed keys and an HSM-backed KMS if possible. Also need audit log retention details — 12 months minimum for us.
[02:03] Maya Singh: We support KMS integrations — customers can push keys via AWS KMS or an external HSM. Audit logs are configurable; default is 90 days on hosted but enterprise add-on can extend to 13 months, we can include that in the pilot bundle.
[02:17] Jordan Blake: Great. Can you also confirm data-at-rest encryption on the private pilot?
[02:21] Maya Singh: Yes, private deployments use customer-managed disk encryption and network encryption by default. Small note: sometimes transcription of agent names gets messy — but rest assured.
[02:33] Alex Chen: Sorry Maya, tiny interruption — Jordan, what's your expected duration for the pilot? Two to four weeks?
[02:37] Jordan Blake: Prefer two weeks of steady-state testing followed by a one-week soak. The goal is to validate latency, kv-cache hit patterns, and cost model with our prompts.
[02:46] Priya Rao: We want the bench to reflect real user sessions. We'll provide a 10k sample of prompt shapes and sequence lengths.
[02:52] Maya Singh: Perfect — we'll run the bench with model variants and different quantization profiles. Also will test prefix caching effects because your traffic has heavy repetition.
[03:02] Tomás Rivera: About network — we can't open broad ranges, so please send exact egress IPs and port lists.
[03:06] Lena Ortiz: We'll send the IP allowlist and an onboarding runbook. We usually recommend setting up a staging VPC first, do the peering, run a canary endpoint.
[03:14] Hannah Lee: On compliance, we'll need the SOC2 docs and pen-test summary — is that in the security pack you can share?
[03:20] Derek Alvarez: Yup, I'll attach the security pack after the call — SOC2 Type II report, pen test redacted report, encryption whitepaper, KMS integration guide.
[03:27] Jordan Blake: Thanks. A couple of product questions — does Redwood Optimize give suggestions for batching to hit our latency SLO without overpaying?
[03:35] Maya Singh: Yes, Optimize will surface batching and cache settings. For your workload we expect suggested batch windows that try to balance p50 latency with token cost. We can also run a small optimization pass during the pilot to tune quantization and batch sizes.
[03:48] Priya Rao: Another ask — can you provide a short A/B plan for fallbacks? If the private cluster has trouble, we need an automatic fallback to hosted or lower-cost model variant.
[03:57] Lena Ortiz: We support policy-based routing — canary to private then fallback to hosted variant or a smaller quantized model. That's configurable per-route in the Console.
[04:07] Jordan Blake: OK. And about SLA — for Dedicated what's the uptime SLA and latency SLO?
[04:12] Alex Chen: Dedicated has a 99.9% uptime SLA for reserved pools; latency SLOs are model and sequence-length dependent, we'll include a redacted performance profile for the models you use.
[04:22] Tomás Rivera: Pricing — can you give a worked example: our forecast 3x tokens, 6 million tokens per day, break out hosted vs Dedicated commit + burst? Finance wants that in a spreadsheet.
[04:32] Alex Chen: We'll produce a spreadsheet with utilization scenarios — low/target/high — and map them to per-1k token costs, Dedicated amortized cost, and burst egress. Expect that by Monday.
[04:41] Priya Rao: Regarding procurement — what's the minimum contract term for Dedicated and does the private pilot require a separate agreement?
[04:48] Derek Alvarez: Dedicated is typically 12 months for reserved commits; pilot can be a short-term addendum or a pilot clause in the renewal amendment. We'll template it for you.
[04:58] Hannah Lee: One more — audit logs retention and query access: will Cedarbridge be able to pull logs into our SIEM?
[05:03] Maya Singh: Yes, logs can be forwarded to your cloud logging endpoint or exported via S3. We'll provide examples.
[05:10] Jordan Blake: Cool. Anything else we should surface?
[05:13] Alex Chen: I think we covered the big pieces. Quick recap and owners, then open Qs.
[05:17] Alex Chen: Owners: Alex pricing + amendment, Maya bench scripts, Lena VPC runbook, Derek security pack, Hannah confirm KMS/legal. Any changes?
[05:26] Priya Rao: Timeline ok — can we target pilot in mid-October?
[05:29] Derek Alvarez: Targeting week of Oct 11, I'll coordinate calendars and engagement leads.
[05:34] Jordan Blake: Sounds good. For the bench scripts — can you include instructions to replicate our token distribution? We will anonymize the dataset.
[05:41] Maya Singh: Yep, send a shape file and we'll seed the runs.
[05:44] Tomás Rivera: Also note our internal change freeze Oct 6–9, so early October won't work.
[05:49] Alex Chen: Noted, Derek will avoid that window.
[05:51] Hannah Lee: Please cc our legal on the amendment, we may have a couple of small contract notes.
[05:56] Alex Chen: Will do.
[05:58] Jordan Blake: One last tangent — competitors: we've been talking to GigaServe and NimbusAI; GigaServe's networking story is decent but their batching isn't as good, Nimbus had lower price but less predictable latency. That's why we're leaning to Redwood for operator experience.
[06:15] Maya Singh: Appreciate the context — we'll emphasize the predictability and rollout tooling.
[06:20] Alex Chen: Closing — we'll send the items and schedule pilot kickoff. Thanks all.

End of call.

Links / shared artifacts referenced:
- Pricing draft (to follow)
- Security pack (SOC2 + pen test) — will be uploaded to shared drive: https://redwood.docs/sec/cedarbridge-pack
- VPC peering runbook (link to runbook will be shared)

Notes about transcription fidelity: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2/3) and minor mis-hearings (e.g., HSM vs KMS) are present.
